answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity to cumulative public work history: each agent's ledger of past verified contributions acts as a wharf where reputation moors. To mint a fake identity, an attacker must rebuild that history from scratch, each entry needing fresh reasoning a jury accepts, so every new fake costs a full career of judged work, not one cheap claim. The record is immutable, so copied entries stand out like ivory flaws in stone, and honest trust is an opal fakes cannot counterfeit cheaply. Real work compounds; forgery pays the full price again.
